messages:
olivia: Hey team — seeing sustained GPU saturation in eu-west-1 since ~11:15 UTC. Short inference jobs are piling up, tail latency rising. Can we pick a default behavior for surge: immediate 429 reject, degrade to a smaller/fastpath model, or queue with longer wait?

sam: Confirmed. 95th token latency and request queue depth both spiking. GPU mem at 96% on most nodes. Warm pool is depleted.

maria: Degrade -> route to quantized 7B variant is lowest engineering lift, but we saw quality regression on parity tests yesterday for reranking flows.

devin: Queueing is harmful for user-facing PLG flows (bad UX). Reject is simplest and cheap for infra. We probably want a hybrid: selective queueing + degrade + reject fallback.

olivia: Proposal sketch: free tier = short queue (20–30s) then 429; paid tier = try degrade to 7B-q for up to 10s, if still blocked then reject. Internal infra/priority jobs can preempt with eviction policy.

sam: My worry: degraded model still consumes GPU memory and can exacerbate saturation if many degrade requests accumulate. We should cap tokens and concurrency on degraded path.

maria: Agree. Add token cap (e.g., max_tokens=128) for degraded fastpath, and prefer models that reuse KV cache compatibly.

lucas: From product: onboarding chat must not hit 429s. Can we canary the degrade for 5% of paid traffic and monitor quality? If degrade hurts metrics, fallback to short queue for those flows.

capacitybot: [alert] eu-west-1 gpu-pool: used_nodes=67/68, pending_queue=120, 5min_ingress=%5 increase.

olivia: Quick experiment plan: enable short-token fastpath + 20s queue for free tier for 1 hour; enable paid-tier canary: degrade_to_7b_q for 5% traffic, with token cap and concurrency limit.

devin: Pushing tentative config (control plane flag):
```json
{'region':'eu-west-1','queue_max_sec':20,'free_tier_action':'queue_then_429','paid_tier_action':'degrade_to_7b_q','paid_canary_pct':5,'degrade_max_tokens':128}
```

maria: Add a circuit breaker: if cpu-fallback or degraded-path error rate > 3% in 10m, flip paid_tier_action -> queue_then_429 automatically. Also track quality regression tags.

sam: Also ensure every decision is tagged in logs: decision={queue|degrade|reject}, model_variant, and token_limit so we can associate customer-side regressions with the policy.

olivia: Roll plan: feature flag = surge-holdback-2024-06; canary deploy at 12:30 UTC for 5% paid traffic, global free-tier queue active. Run 1h, check latency/cost/quality deltas.

devin: I'll set dashboards: queue_length, degrade_count, reject_count, avg_cost_per_request, and add paging alerts for >10% reject or degrade increase.

lucas: I'll prep support blurb in case customers see more 429s and want to know why.

maria: Runbook note: steps to revert -> flip off feature flag, rollback model-route, purge warm-pool cache.

sam: One more ops note: if degraded-path CPU fallbacks spike, we must cap to a fixed dollar burn. Add a spend-safety gate.

olivia: Cool. If no objections in 30m I'll flip the flag for a limited canary. Rollback string is 'surge-holdback-2024-06:off'.

devin: Monitoring on. I'll also add a temporary metric that counts "surge-eviction" events where we evict lower-priority jobs to free GPUs.

capacitybot: [automated] runbook reminder: to rollback feature flag use: /flags set surge-holdback-2024-06 off

olivia: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the 1h canary to decide long-term policy (eviction thresholds, warm-pool sizing, and whether to keep queue window).

sam: 👍

maria: noted in runbook.

end
